options: Which workspace a report can be published to
Which rows of data a role's members see, based on a DAX filter
Whether a user can edit a report versus only view it
Which sensitivity label is applied to a dataset
questions.explain: RLS attaches a DAX filter expression to a role, restricting which rows of underlying data that role's members see — two people can view the identical report and see different numbers.

questions.q: Where is an RLS role's DAX filter expression actually written?
options: In the Power BI service's tenant settings
In the workspace's Manage access pane
In Power BI Desktop, on the Manage roles dialog, before publishing
It is generated automatically from the report's visuals
questions.explain: Roles and their DAX filter expressions are defined in Power BI Desktop. Assigning actual people or groups to an already-defined role happens afterward, in the Power BI service.

questions.q: What happens if a role is published with zero members assigned in the Power BI service?
options: The DAX filter applies to every user in the tenant by default
Power BI automatically deletes the unused role
The role's filter enforces nothing, since no one is actually assigned to it
The semantic model fails to publish until a member is added
questions.explain: A role with no members doesn't restrict anyone's data — RLS only takes effect for users or groups actually added as members of that role.

questions.q: What does the 'Test as role' / 'View as' feature verify?
options: Whether a scheduled refresh is configured correctly
How a role's RLS filter actually behaves, by impersonating a role or a specific person
Whether a gateway connection is required
Which endorsement badge a dataset qualifies for
questions.explain: Test as role / View as lets you confirm what a role (or a specific person within it) actually sees under the applied DAX filter, before trusting it in production.

questions.q: How does row-level security differ from a workspace role like Viewer?
options: They are the same control, just named differently in Desktop versus the service
Workspace roles only apply to dashboards, while RLS only applies to reports
A Viewer workspace role has no concept of data at all
A Viewer workspace role controls access to content items; RLS additionally filters which rows of data within that content a person sees
questions.explain: Workspace roles (Admin/Member/Contributor/Viewer) control who can access content at all. RLS is a separate, independent layer that filters which rows of data a viewer sees within content they already have access to.
